title: Global Banking Annual Review 2026
figure_ref: Exhibit 5 — expected change in global banking ROE 2025–2028 (editorial waterfall)
business_context: McKinsey describes structural pressures and opportunities facing the global banking industry. Its Exhibit 5 models 2025 ROE of 13% plus passive tailwinds of 2.3pp and active initiatives of a further 1.4pp by 2028. The increments are modeled contributions, not audited realized returns.
key_message: In a modeled scenario, banking ROE could rise from 13% to 15.3% through passive effects and to 16.7% with an additional 1.4pp active premium.
so_what: Executives should separate externally available tailwinds from the incremental impact of active capital allocation before setting 2028 ROE targets.
original_chart_type: Original chart not visually verified (web exhibit accessible in prose only)
encoding: x=baseline and forecast scenario components; y=ROE%; colors=baseline,increments,total; floating contributions

values.label: Active premium
values.denominator: Average incremental benefit from active capital deployment

data_recipe: Record the historical 2025 ROE baseline and set the same denominator of equity in all periods.
Extract passive and active modeled ROE changes in percentage points, not relative percent growth.
Calculate intermediary scenario 13 + 2.3 = 15.3 and 2028 active scenario 15.3 + 1.4 = 16.7.
In a waterfall, render increments from the prior total and the final total from zero.
Distinguish observed 2025 baseline from conditional modeled 2028 increments; verify assumptions before adoption.
message_conditions: The +2.3pp and +1.4pp values describe modeled average scenarios, not realized sector performance.
The apparent 16.7% is derived by addition; source warns that rounded components can differ slightly.
No bank-level distribution or confidence interval is available; neither increment is guaranteed.
Avoid equating global modeled returns with returns to an individual bank.
design_moves: Kind waterfall; color/layout/context configurable via THEME and CONTEXT
Direct labels and careful unit/denominator distinction
All positions computed from data and series order
